channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: Egypt Traffic Fines and Violations Guide
item.description: Traffic fines in Egypt are issued electronically through smart cameras and traffic police, with penalties ranging from small fees to vehicle impoundment.

item.title: Egypt Electricity and Utility Bills: A Practical Guide
item.description: Electricity, water, and gas in Egypt are billed by state-run utility companies, with electricity priced on a tiered scale based on monthly consumption.

item.title: Food Allergies vs Food Intolerances: What's the Difference
item.description: A food allergy involves the immune system and can be life-threatening, while a food intolerance is a digestive issue that causes discomfort but isn't dangerous.

item.title: The History of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina
item.description: The Prophet's Mosque in Medina was built in 622 CE by Prophet Muhammad himself and has grown from a simple structure into one of Islam's holiest sites.

item.title: How Al-Azhar's Islamic Education System Works
item.description: Al-Azhar operates a parallel education track in Egypt, from primary school through university, combining religious and modern academic subjects.

item.title: How Do APIs Work? The Bridge That Lets Apps Talk
item.description: An API is a defined set of rules that lets one piece of software request data or functions from another, acting as a structured bridge between programs.

item.title: How Do Volcanoes Actually Erupt?
item.description: Volcanic eruptions happen when molten rock, gas, and pressure inside the Earth build up until they force their way through a weak point in the crust.

item.title: How Gold Prices Are Determined Globally
item.description: Gold's global price is set through continuous trading on international markets, driven by central bank demand, the US dollar, and investor sentiment.

item.title: How Import Tariffs Actually Work
item.description: An import tariff is a tax a government charges on goods entering the country, usually collected from the importer at customs before goods are released.

item.title: How National Lottery Draws Actually Work
item.description: Lottery draws use certified random number generators or physical ball machines, with independent auditors and public draws designed to prove fairness.

item.title: The Legend of Anansi the Spider
item.description: Anansi is a clever trickster spider from West African folklore who outwits stronger characters through wit rather than strength, and became a Caribbean folk hero too.

item.title: The Legend of Beowulf
item.description: Beowulf is an Old English epic poem about a hero who defeats the monster Grendel, and it's one of the oldest surviving works of English literature.

item.title: The Legend of the Kraken
item.description: The Kraken is a legendary sea monster from Scandinavian folklore, said to be large enough to be mistaken for an island before dragging ships underwater.

item.title: The History of Mosaic Art
item.description: Mosaic art, made from small pieces of stone, glass, or tile, dates back over 4,000 years and spread across cultures from Mesopotamia to Byzantium.

item.title: Understanding Compassion Fatigue
item.description: Compassion fatigue is the emotional exhaustion that can affect people who repeatedly care for others in distress, common among caregivers and helpers.

item.title: Understanding the Barnum Effect
item.description: The Barnum effect describes why people rate vague, generic personality descriptions as highly accurate, believing they were written specifically for them.

item.title: What Causes Earthquakes?
item.description: Earthquakes happen when built-up stress along fault lines suddenly releases, sending seismic waves through the ground as tectonic plates shift.

item.title: What Is 5G and How Is It Different From 4G?
item.description: 5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology, offering significantly faster speeds and lower latency than 4G through new radio frequencies.

item.title: What Is a Trade Deficit?
item.description: A trade deficit happens when a country imports more goods and services in value than it exports, and it isn't automatically a sign of economic weakness.

item.title: What Is a VPN and How Does It Work?
item.description: A VPN encrypts your internet traffic and routes it through a remote server, masking your real location and protecting your data on public networks.
